title: Caesar summons German horsemen
source_critical_note: Caesar reports calling for cavalry and light infantry across the Rhine (arcessit); this is external recruitment, not evidence for a territorial foedus.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Agrippa transfers the Ubii
source_critical_note: Strabo reports Agrippa's relocation of the Ubii with their consent; the exact year is uncertain, and a military treaty is not documented.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete
date_label_es: Finales del siglo I a. C.

title: Plautius Silvanus and the Transdanubians
source_critical_note: CIL XIV 3608 = ILS 986 uses transduxit and refers to tribute obligations. Whether it records a physical relocation or another form of Roman control is debated. The linked publication discusses the inscription; it is not the epigraphic edition itself.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Iazyges cavalry dispatched to Britain
source_critical_note: Cassius Dio describes a peace obligation of 8,000 Iazyges horsemen, 5,500 sent to Britain. This does not establish voluntary invitation or collective settlement.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Probus settles Bastarnae in Thrace
source_critical_note: Zosimus 1.71.1 reports granting land to Bastarnae in Thrace, but provides no secure exact year or full settlement terms.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Probus grants land to Franks
source_critical_note: Zosimus 1.71.2 describes a Frankish petition and grant, followed by a violent departure. The exact year and settlement district are not securely identifiable.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Procopius obtains Gothic support
source_critical_note: Ammianus records 3,000 Goths and a letter attributed to Procopius; Zosimus reports 10,000. These conflicting numerical traditions must not be harmonised silently.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Valens admits the Tervingi
source_critical_note: Ammianus narrates a petition from the Tervingi, Valens's authorisation and the crossing. The Greuthungi were not covered by this authorisation.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Theodosius receives Athanaric
source_critical_note: Reception and funeral attested; not collective permanent settlement.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Roman-Gothic peace arrangements
source_critical_note: Themistius' ceremonial oration celebrates peace; no surviving treaty specifies the precise legal, fiscal and territorial clauses often ascribed to the 382 settlement.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Alan contingent protects Bazas
source_critical_note: Paulinus of Pella reports negotiation with an Alan king during the siege of Bazas. This was local military realignment, not a new frontier entry; the king's identification is contested.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Goths campaign for Rome then settle
source_critical_note: Wallia's campaigning in Hispania and subsequent settlement in Aquitaine belong to different stages and testimonies; the land/fiscal arrangements are debated.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Bonifatius allegedly calls the Vandals
source_critical_note: Procopius attributes a call for Vandal aid to Bonifatius; the 429 crossing is attested, but Prosper does not identify Bonifatius personally as the inviter.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Alans assigned land at Valence
source_critical_note: The Gallic Chronicle of 452 (124) records allocation of deserted land in the Valence region to Alans under Sambida. The Roman granting officer is not named.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Aetius allocates land to Alans
source_critical_note: Gallic Chronicle of 452 (127) credits Aetius with the grant and reports forceful eviction of resisting landowners; Roman authorisation did not entail local consent.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Burgundians allocated Sapaudia
source_critical_note: Gallic Chronicle of 452 (128) records Sapaudia being granted to Burgundian survivors for division with its inhabitants; no named Roman grantor or precise treaty clauses survive.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Eudoxia allegedly summons Gaiseric
source_critical_note: Hydatius explicitly reports the alleged appeal by Eudoxia as rumour (ut mala fama dispergit). The sack of Rome is attested; the alleged invitation is not corroborated.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Zeno commissions Theoderic against Odoacer
source_critical_note: Procopius relates Zeno's suggestion that Theoderic displace Odoacer. The constitutional authority of the later Italian regime cannot be deduced solely from this report.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Justinian recruits Lombards and Heruls
source_critical_note: Procopius 8.26 distinguishes the Lombard alliance negotiated with Audoin from Herul participation under their own commanders. Do not combine these into a single foedus.
editorial_stage: v0.2.1: source-critical notes revised using the 20-case audit; critical-edition and historiographical collation incomplete

title: Maurice finances a Frankish expedition
primary_source: Gregory of Tours, Histories 6.42; John of Biclaro s.a. 584
source_critical_note: Gregory describes 50,000 solidi received some years previously (ante hos annos) and a Frankish campaign followed by peace with the Lombards. Payment and campaign must not be assigned an identical exact date.
